The pair join the likes of BBC content boss Kate Phillips and Sky Studios CEO Cécile Frot-Coutaz on the governors board. They bring together film and TV production expertise with digital as the school continues to evolve, according to the NFTS. Double Oscar nominee Harris is the founder of Neal Street and has been behind the likes of 1917, Call the Midwife and Hamnet. Upcoming she has Sam Mendes’ quartet of Beatles movies. As YouTube UK and Ireland boss for nearly four years, Lomax occupies a different lane. She has overseen serious growth for the Google-owned platform in the UK and has impressed traditional TV executives along the way. Related Stories News YouTube Ad Revenue Rises 9% But Parent Alphabet Misses Wall Street's Q3 Targets; Stock Drops News Entertainment Hits $332.5B To Become World's Second Most Valuable Sector As Netflix, YouTube & Spotify Fly - Interbrand Report Alongside Harris, Lomax, Phillips and Frot-Coutaz, the NFTS board is comprised of Roughcut TV founder Ash Atalla , Film4 Director Farhana Bhula, ITV Studios MD Julian Bellamy and ex-Warner Bros. Discovery VP Polly Cochrane. Watch on Deadline The appointments come at a significant moment for the NFTS as it prepares to open The Cubby Broccoli Building at its Beaconsfield HQ in January 2027. title: TBS Unpacks Collaborations With Legendary & Korea’s CJ ENM: “We Want To Create A New Global Genre Of J-Content”
full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027 ‘Merry Berry Love’ Producers Nippon TV & CJ ENM Talk Korea-Japan Collaboration To Boost J-Drama – TIFFCOM Amazon MGM Studios Japan To Double Investment In Original Content; ‘One Piece’ & ‘Kingdom’ Producers Talk IP Strategies – TIFFCOM View All October 29, 2026 2:23am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Alice In Borderland Season 3 The Seven, Netflix TBS Holdings executives outlined the strategy behind the Japanese broadcaster’s tie-ups with Legendary Entertainment and Korea’s CJ ENM in a TIFFCOM presentation today. In January 2026, TBS acquired a $150M minority stake in Legendary and entered into a non-exclusive agreement with the Dune and Godzilla franchise producer to source and develop Japanese IP. Katsuaki Setoguchi, TBS Holdings Executive Officer, Global Business Division, opened the presentation by explaining why the Japanese broadcaster made this move: “Why did we partner with Legendary? Our needs matched each other perfectly.” Related Stories News Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027 News Toho CEO Matsuoka Hiro On The Company's Decision To Self-Distribute 'Godzilla Minus One' In The U.S. -- Tokyo He continued that Legendary has been “keeping a close eye on Japanese IP” and as the Godzilla franchise and other projects have proved, are willing to invest in big-budget live-action adaptations. In addition to Godzilla , the company is producing several theatrical and episodic projects based on Japanese IP, including Street Fighter, Gundam and Drops Of God Season 2 . Watch on Deadline “They needed upfront investment and to tie up with Japanese IP holders, but also had to understand the soul of the original work,” Setoguchi said. “Finding partners you can develop a deep relationship with is difficult. But TBS has long-standing relationships with many creators for live-action works, so working together with us, they could deliver Japanese IP to the rest of the world.” Setoguchi also said TBS has “neutral” relationships with all the major publishers in Japan, so isn’t limited to working with specific rights holders. He added that, starting this month, TBS employees will be setting up desks in the Legendary offices in Los Angeles to ensure a close working relationship. TBS already has its own offices in LA, and an outpost of its international production outfit The Seven, which has produced shows including three seasons of Alice In Borderland and Did Someone Happen To Mention Me , starring Koji Yakusho, both of which are streaming on Netflix, and Prime Original Rock Paper Landmine . Meanwhile, back in Asia, TBS has been forming similar tie-ups, launching a production joint venture Studio Monowa with Korea’s CJ ENM and Japanese streamer UNEXT, with announcements on the first projects expected soon. The aim for TBS is to propel Japanese drama to the same level of global recognition as Korean dramas. He observed that while K-drama is widely distributed to international markets, Japanese live-action content is not as well known, although anime and manga are hugely popular nearly everywhere in the world. Setoguchi recalled that one of the first shows co-produced by Japan and Korea was 2002 drama Friends – produced by TBS and Korea’s MBC – which was created to commemorate the 2002 FIFA World Cup co-hosted by South Korea and Japan. He described the show as “the first time Japanese was spoken on Korean TV since the war”. He added that, back then, Japan’s TV drama industry was much stronger than Korea’s and that Korean production staff were “enthusiastic to absorb every aspect of Japanese production expertise”. “We thought that since there’s a huge gap in production capabilities, it would be difficult for Korean teams to create global hits. More than 20 years have passed and we all know how that has turned out. Japan pursued domestic viewer ratings, while Korea looked at global markets, and those decisions have shaped today’s reality. We feel our mission now is to create a new global genre of J-Content.” On the unscripted side, TBS has built a global industry around the Ninja Warrior format, working with partners including Banijay, RTL and ITV Studio, who all appeared via video clips during the TIFFCOM presentation to talk about the strengths of the format. Banijay is selling the Israeli version of the show, which is returning after a three-year hiatus, while Australia is bringing it back after five years. Noting that sports-related programming is having a resurgence, Banijay Chief Content Officer James Townley said: “With the Olympics coming up, Ninja Warrior can capitalize on the strength of that and will be a major focus for us across Europe next year.” TIFFCOM is running for three days (October 28-30) at the Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center in Hamamatsucho. It will launch on Australia on DAZN’s Binge and in the UK on 5 later this year. “Katrina, Nicole and Kate have created globally iconic characters and I am delighted they are returning to start a new chapter outside of Wentworth Prison, alongside brand new characters viewers will learn to love and hate,” said Greg Barnett, Commissioning Editor at 5. “The ultimate prize is their permanent freedom. It’s not about getting out, it’s about staying out. Beyond Bars is intense and relentless in its twists and turns. Loyal Wentworth Prison fans and new viewers will be on the edge of their seats.” Jamie Lynn, EVP Co-Production & Distribution, EMEA, Commercial and International at Fremantle, added: “ Wentworth has become an enduring global drama franchise with an incredibly loyal fanbase, and Beyond Bars marks an exciting new chapter. title: Mayur More & Ashlesha Thakur To Lead ‘Beta Builder’, Debut Hybrid AI Feature From Abundantia AiOn & InVideo
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members Disney+ & Netflix Hoover Up Non-English Acquisitions As Fervor For Japanese & Korean Content Continues – Ampere View All October 29, 2026 2:43am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mayur More and Ashlesha Thakur Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Mayur More and Ashlesha Thakur will star in the first AI-driven feature film from the pact between India ‘s Abundantia Entertainment and video tech firm InVideo . Beta Builder has InVideo’s Global Creative Lead, Hridaye A. Nagpal, attached to direct, with principal photography beginning today in Mumbai. The Indian city will, per the producers, serve “as both its home and creative starting point.” Abundantia is producing through its Abundantia AiOn division, which was formed last year as an AI production division framed as “human-first and AI-empowered.” Last year, it partnered with Sanket Shah’s San Francisco-headquartered InVideo on a slate of five AI-powered films launched over three years with a ₹100 crore ($10.5M) commitment behind it. Related Stories News Zee Studios Sets Release Date For Omung Kumar's 'Silaa' News Prime Video Adds Sony LIV To Indian Offer Beta Builder will tell the story of Jai, a self-taught, genius architect from Dharavi, a densely populated area of Mumbai, who “gets a chance to realize his dreams in the world of virtual reality), only to discover that winning means far more than proving himself. An underdog in every sense, Jai must fight the system that holds him back, win the love of his life, and give his community a voice in shaping its own future.” Watch on Deadline Producers say it is “rooted in one of India’s most iconic geographies and set against the limitless possibilities of a virtual world,” with the story exploring “ambition, belonging and what it truly means to build something that lasts.” The film is being positioned as a hybrid production, “pairing full-blown, live-action filming with AI-driven production,” and More ( Kotak Factory & Black , White & Gray: Love kills ) is starring alongside Thakur ( The Family Man ). “We are about to see a wave of fascinating films,” said director Nagpal. “With AI-assisted filmmaking, storytellers can dream much bigger, and backing a bold idea finally feels possible. The partnership between Abundantia and InVideo gives filmmakers the scale and creative support to take on ideas like this. Beta Builder is our bet on that future, with a live-action shoot and AI working side by side” Last month, Abundantia founder and CEO Vikram Malhotra outlined his vision for using AI in production in an interview with Deadline, while revealing Abundantia AiOn was morphing into a fully native standalone AI studio. He has sought to find the balance between the opportunity of AI and the “The capability needed to run AI at studio level will not be found solely within the conventional media and entertainment system,” he said at the time. “It is truly a confluence of technology and art.” Today, he said in a statement: “In our partnership with InVideo and Sanket, our focus is to leverage AI and tell stories that are unique, impactful and entertaining. I am delighted that the first film in our slate is one that tells a story set in a relatable, young world and explores aspirational possibilities beyond. “In Hridaye, we have a filmmaker who combines a strong creative vision with a deep command over technology, which makes him the ideal person to lead and bring Beta Builder to life. I am excited about how AiOn is enabling unique stories and storytellers to come to the fore and bring their best to fans all over the world.” “At InVideo, our mission has always been to put powerful tools in the hands of storytellers,” added Shah, CEO of InVideo. “ Beta Builder is where that mission takes the form of a full-length film, made with a partner of Abundantia’s calibre. It is a story about building something that lasts, which makes it the right film to begin this slate with.” Abundantia is known for the likes of Prime Video series Breathe and Daldal , Netflix crime-comedy Maa Behen , Baby , Toiler – Ek Prem Katha , Chhorii and Subedaar , the action thriller starring Anil Kapoor. InVideo, which is U.S.-based with offices in India, positions itself as a agnostic AI filmmaking platform with more than 50 million users. Its backers include Peak XV, Tiger Global, Greenoaks, RTP Global, Base Partners, and Hummingbird. title: ‘The Cube’ Creator Adam Adler Joins Channel 4’s Production Biz As Creative Director
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series ‘The Cube’ Creator Adam Adler Joins Channel 4’s Production Biz As Creative Director Pippa Harris & YouTube UK Boss Alison Lomax Join Board Of National Film & Television School View All October 29, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Cube' TBS EXCLUSIVE: Sarah Dillistone has made her first big hire at Channel 4 ’s in-house production biz. Dillistone has snapped up The Cube creator Adam Adler as Creative Director and he will lead on the creation of new shows for the nascent unit. Adler is a highly-regarded British formats executive who is best known as creator of ITV’s The Cube , which ran for 11 seasons and nearly 100 episodes beween 2009 and 2021. An American version aired for three seasons on TBS. Adler’s other creations include Bar Wars and The Games, while he has most recently been EPing Channel 4’s upcoming Derren Brown: Incognito. He is a former Channel 4 entertainment commissioner and also ran an indie, Gameface, before moving to ITV Studios-owned label Potato. Related Stories News Disney+ & Channel 4 Strike Landmark Deal In UK News Nicola Coughlan's 'I Am Helen' Trailer Shows Dark Side Of Modern Relationships As Toxic Masculinity Takes Its Toll Channel 4’s in-house production biz emerged from the UK government’s botched attempt to sell off the broadcaster and is one way in which the Gogglebox network can forge IP, which can then be sold around the world. The unit, which Channel 4 says is separated from its commissioning team by a “clear operational firewall,” unveiled ex- Made in Chelsea showrunner Dillistone as its lead at the start of 2026. She relocated to London from L.A., where she spent six years making shows like Perfect Match and The Ultimatum. Watch on Deadline More updates on the creative and development side of Channel 4 in-house are expected soon. Dillistone called Adler an “unrivalled creative force.” “He is one of the most prolific format creators around spanning gameshow, reality and entertainment,” she added. “Adam’s experience originating ambitious and unpredictable formats from The Cube to Channel 4’s brand new reality series Incognito , coupled with my own background originating and showrunning reality, social experiments and relationship shows, makes for an exciting mix.” Adler added: “I’m really excited to be joining Dilly at the start of this new venture. Channel 4 has always had attitude and originality, and I’d love us to bottle some of that up and take it out into the world. The ambition is to create exciting ideas with that same spirit, for TV and beyond.” In other Channel 4 news, highly-rated docs chief Alisa Pomeroy has taken on the top head of unscripted job amid the restructure that is seeing around half of commissioners laid off. Pomeroy’s fiefdom has expanded vastly and she is now looking after documentaries, factual entertainment, reality, entertainment and specialist factual. A day before Pomeroy’s promotion, Broadcast reported that comedy boss Charlie Perkins and entertainment chief Steve Handley are leaving. A scripted supremo looking after both drama and comedy is expected to be appointed in the coming months. title: Russell Brand’s Wife Says Star Was “Caring” Lover At Time Of Rape Allegations
full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Russell Brand’s Wife Says Star Was “Caring” Lover At Time Of Rape Allegations BAFTA Launches Review Over Concerns About Trustees Accepting Free Awards Guest Tickets BBC “Disappointed” As Staff Plan Industrial Action Vote Over Job Cuts View All October 29, 2026 4:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand and wife, Laura Brand, arrive at Southwark Crown Court Getty Russell Brand ‘s wife has told a court that the Despicable Me star was a caring and considerate lover during the period in which he has been accused of rape. Laura Brand took to the witness stand on Thursday at London’s Southwark Crown Court, giving evidence in support of her husband, who faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one of attempted indecent assault. The charges span a 10-year period from 1999 to 2009. Laura Brand told the court that she first met Russell in August 2006 after a gig in Edinburgh, and they began a sexual relationship a month later. Asked what kind of lover Russell was, Laura said he was “very caring” and went at “my pace.” She added: “I felt entirely cared for and looked after by Russell.” Related Stories News Prosecution Rejects Russell Brand's Claim He Has Been Abandoned: "You Have A Platform Of Millions" Legal Russell Brand Forcefully Denies Charges As He Gives Evidence During Rape Trial: "Consent Is More Important Than Sex Itself" The pair broke up in February 2007 after Russell was unfaithful. “I was not interested in having a relationship with him if he was sleeping with other people — it was really difficult for him to be in a monogamous relationship,” Laura said. “I was a little heartbroken.” Watch on Deadline Riel Karmy-Jones, the prosecution barrister, pointed out that Laura was not in a relationship with Russell in 2009, when Complainant 5 alleged that she was anally raped by the Forgetting Sarah Marshall actor. Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began. Russell and Laura reconnected a decade later, marrying in 2017 near Henley-on-Thames in Oxfordshire. They have three children together. Laura, who has been in court most days, described her husband as being “amazingly attentive” and “kind,” telling jurors: “I love him very much.” Two of Brand’s ex-girlfriends also gave evidence through witness statements that were read out in court by a defense lawyer. One woman, who dated Brand between 1996 and 1999, said he was “gentle and loving.” The second, who had an open relationship with Brand from 1999, added: “He never engaged in an intimate act without mutual consent.” Both said he was promiscuous, with the second noting that “women would circle like birds” around Brand as he became more famous. The prosecution and defense have now made their case to the jury. Closing arguments are expected tomorrow. The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, expects the jury to begin verdict deliberations next Tuesday, November 3. title: Disney+ & Netflix Hoover Up Non-English Acquisitions As Fervor For Japanese & Korean Content Continues – Ampere
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Bella Glanville Signs With Established Artists ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members View All October 29, 2026 4:42am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix drama 'Alice in Borderland' Netflix Disney+ and Netflix ‘s buying habits appear to be dispelling the notion that non-English-language acquisitions aren’t on their agendas. Research from Ampere Analysis shows that non-English content now accounts for at least half of acquisitions at both global streamers. As of September, non-English content accounted for 65% of Netflix acquisitions, with the figure at Disney+ hitting 50%. Japan and Korea were the leading source for Netflix acquisitions, with German and Japanese content topping Disney+’s list. Related Stories News Cannes Marché & TIFFCOM Commit To Holding Second Edition Of Japan IP Market In 2027 Books Everything We Know About Netflix's New 'Pride & Prejudice' Series So Far Ampere noted its research had identified Japanese, French, South Korean and Turkish as the biggest acquisition opportunities moving forwards if high demand and relatively low export volume was considered. Just 40% of Japanese streaming content is available worldwide, with the U.S. and South Korea the biggest buyers of what can be bought, though France and Germany also show relatively high interest. Watch on Deadline It’s a similar story for South Korean content – despite the global popularity of K-drama, only 45% of the country’s titles are available only on its own streaming services. The Middle East and Southeast Asia appear most likely to bite on its romantic-themed films and shows, Ampere claimed. “Non-English content remains underexploited despite growing global demand. In recent years, Amazon Prime Video, HBO Max and Disney+ have increasingly expanded non-English-language title licensing in multiple markets,” said Tingting Li, Research Manager at Ampere. “Japanese, South Korean, French and Turkish content present the top opportunities for international licensing, with strong audience appeal but still gaps in cross-border availability. title: European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Bella Glanville Signs With Established Artists ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role As Full Trailer Drops For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Series European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members View All October 29, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Canada and Europe have been moving closer politically Getty Canada and Europe have been moving closer together politically, and now their media production bodies are doing the same. CEPI , the European Audiovisual Production Association, has welcomed the Canadian Media Producers Association (CMPA) and the Association Québécoise de la Production Médiatique (AQPM) as its first international observer members. CEPI represents 3,000 independent production companies in 17 countries through 19 national associations and one European association, and now counts the two Canadian bodies among its ranks. Related Stories News Hudson Williams, Zach Galifianakis & Jay Baruchel Set For 'The Assembly' Season 2 At Canada's CBC News Raven Banner Boards Polish Folklore Horror 'Òpi' Ahead Of U.S. Festival Debut The European Union and Canada have moved closer politically together during the Trump Presidency, and their media bodies have followed suit, with CBC/Radio-Canada the first non-European network to become a full member of the European Broadcasting Union over the summer and Canada set to compete in the next Eurovision Song Contest. Watch on Deadline CEPI will work with the CMPA and AQPM to strengthen dialog and coordinate on shared advocacy issues such as regulation of streaming services, domestic production requirements, IP and rights, and co-productions. The news comes after the three bodes and other producer associations from Australia and across Europe signed a joint statement calling on governments to protect domestic production and local storytelling at the Toronto International Film Festival last month. “The arrival of CMPA and AQPM as CEPI’s first international observer members reflects the increasingly international nature of the audiovisual industry,” said Anthony Muldoon, President of CEPI. “While Europe and Canada may be an ocean apart, the challenges and opportunities facing our independent production sectors are remarkably similar. We share a commitment to supporting independent producers and creating original stories that reflect our respective cultural realities.” CMPA President and CEO Reynolds Mastin added: “Canadian and European independent producers face many of the same challenges, from modernizing regulations for the digital age to ensuring that local stories continue to be told, and to making sure domestic producers have a fair opportunity to own their work. We are stronger when we tackle these challenges together.” Hélène Messier, President and Executive Director at AQPM, called joining CEPI “a great privilege,” as she flagged challenges such as generative AI, diversity of cultural expression and preservation of cultural sovereignty. ‘The Diplomat’ Renewed For Season 5 At Netflix, Two Weeks After S4 Arrival Marcus Theatres Posts Record Q3 Led By ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ Amid Boom Skydance Sets Leadership Team For Studios, Entertainment, News & Sports Gregory Nava Mourns Civil Rights Leader Delores Huerta, Updates On Biopic Plans Read More About: Comments
